## Problem 1

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(MatchIt)   # For propensity score matching
library(survey)    # For IPW and survey-weighted analysis
library(broom)     # For tidy model output
library(causaldata) # For the NHEFS dataset

# Load the NHEFS dataset
data("nhefs", package = "causaldata")

# Covariates to adjust for
covariates <- c("sex", "race", "age", "education", "smokeintensity", "smokeyrs", 
                "exercise", "active", "wt71", "hbp")

# Step 1: Fit a logistic regression model to calculate propensity scores
ps_model <- glm(qsmk ~ sex + race + age + education + smokeintensity + smokeyrs +
                exercise + active + wt71 + hbp, family = binomial(), data = nhefs)

# Generate propensity scores
nhefs$pscore <- predict(ps_model, type = "response")

# Outcomes to consider
outcome_vars <- c("wt82_71", "sbp", "dbp")
outcome_desc <- c("Weight change (1971-1982)", "Systolic Blood Pressure", "Diastolic Blood Pressure")


### (a) Correct Regression Adjustment with Covariates

calculate_att_covariates <- function(outcome_var) {
  # Fit regression model on the full dataset with treatment and covariates
  model <- lm(as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ qsmk +", paste(covariates, collapse = " + "))), data = nhefs)
  
  # Extract the treatment effect (ATT) from the regression model
  result <- tidy(model) %>% filter(term == "qsmk")
  return(list(estimate = result$estimate, std_error = result$std.error))
}

# Apply regression adjustment with covariates to all outcomes
att_covariates <- lapply(outcome_vars, calculate_att_covariates)

### (b) Correct Regression Adjustment with Propensity Score

calculate_att_pscore <- function(outcome_var) {
  # Fit regression model with propensity score as an additional covariate
  model <- lm(as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ qsmk + pscore")), data = nhefs)
  
  # Extract the treatment effect (ATT) from the regression model
  result <- tidy(model) %>% filter(term == "qsmk")
  return(list(estimate = result$estimate, std_error = result$std.error))
}

# Apply regression adjustment with propensity score to all outcomes
att_pscore <- lapply(outcome_vars, calculate_att_pscore)

### (c) Correct Propensity Score Stratification

calculate_att_stratification <- function(outcome_var) {
  # Stratify based on the propensity score into quintiles
  nhefs$strata <- cut(nhefs$pscore, breaks = quantile(nhefs$pscore, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.2)), 
                      include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
  
  strat_results <- list()
  for (stratum in unique(nhefs$strata)) {
    stratum_data <- nhefs %>% filter(strata == stratum)
    
    # Fit a regression model within each stratum
    model <- lm(as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ qsmk")), data = stratum_data)
    result <- tidy(model) %>% filter(term == "qsmk")
    strat_results[[stratum]] <- result$estimate
  }
  
  # Aggregate results across strata to get the overall ATT
  overall_att <- mean(unlist(strat_results))
  return(list(estimate = overall_att))
}

# Apply propensity score stratification to all outcomes
att_stratification <- lapply(outcome_vars, calculate_att_stratification)

### (d) Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW)

calculate_att_ipw <- function(outcome_var) {
  # Calculate ATT weights
  nhefs$weights <- ifelse(nhefs$qsmk == 1, 1, nhefs$pscore / (1 - nhefs$pscore))
  
  # Survey design object
  design <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~weights, data = nhefs)
  
  # Fit weighted regression
  model <- svyglm(as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ qsmk")), design = design)
  result <- tidy(model) %>% filter(term == "qsmk")
  return(list(estimate = result$estimate, std_error = result$std.error))
}

# Apply inverse probability weighting to all outcomes
att_ipw <- lapply(outcome_vars, calculate_att_ipw)

### (e) Propensity Score Matching (1:1 and 2:1)

calculate_att_matching <- function(outcome_var, ratio = 1) {
  # Propensity score matching
  match_model <- matchit(qsmk ~ sex + race + age + education + smokeintensity + smokeyrs +
                         exercise + active + wt71 + hbp, data = nhefs, method = "nearest", ratio = ratio)
  
  matched_data <- match.data(match_model)
  
  # Fit regression on matched data
  model <- lm(as.formula(paste(outcome_var, "~ qsmk")), data = matched_data)
  result <- tidy(model) %>% filter(term == "qsmk")
  return(list(estimate = result$estimate, std_error = result$std.error))
}

# 1:1 matching
att_matching_1to1 <- lapply(outcome_vars, calculate_att_matching, ratio = 1)

# 2:1 matching
att_matching_2to1 <- lapply(outcome_vars, calculate_att_matching, ratio = 2)


### Print Results for Each Method and Outcome

print_results <- function(att, method_name) {
  for (i in seq_along(outcome_vars)) {
    cat(paste0(method_name, " ATT for ", outcome_desc[i], ":\n"))
    cat("- Estimate: ", att[[i]]$estimate, "\n")
    if (!is.null(att[[i]]$std_error)) {
      cat("- Standard Error: ", att[[i]]$std_error, "\n")
    }
    cat("\n")
  }
}

cat("\n(a) Regression Adjustment with Covariates:\n")
print_results(att_covariates, "(a)")

cat("\n(b) Regression Adjustment with Propensity Score:\n")
print_results(att_pscore, "(b)")

cat("\n(c) Propensity Score Stratification:\n")
print_results(att_stratification, "(c)")

cat("\n(d) Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW):\n")
print_results(att_ipw, "(d)")

cat("\n(e) Propensity Score Matching (1:1):\n")
print_results(att_matching_1to1, "(e) 1:1 Matching")

cat("\n(e) Propensity Score Matching (2:1):\n")
print_results(att_matching_2to1, "(e) 2:1 Matching")


```
## Problem 2

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(MatchIt)   # For propensity score matching
library(cobalt)    # For balance diagnostics
library(survey)    # For inverse probability weighting
library(dplyr)     # For data manipulation
library(ggplot2)   # For plotting
library(tidyr)     # For pivot_longer()

# Load the NHEFS dataset
library(causaldata)
data("nhefs", package = "causaldata")

# Define covariates
covariates <- c("sex", "race", "age", "education", "smokeintensity", "smokeyrs", 
                "exercise", "active", "wt71", "hbp")

# Step 1: Fit a logistic regression model to calculate propensity scores
ps_model <- glm(qsmk ~ sex + race + age + education + smokeintensity + smokeyrs +
                exercise + active + wt71 + hbp, family = binomial(), data = nhefs)

# Add propensity scores to the dataset
nhefs$pscore <- predict(ps_model, type = "response")

### (A) Propensity Score Matching (1:1 matching)

# Perform 1:1 nearest-neighbor propensity score matching, keeping unmatched individuals
match_model <- matchit(qsmk ~ sex + race + age + education + smokeintensity + smokeyrs +
                       exercise + active + wt71 + hbp, data = nhefs, method = "nearest", ratio = 1, 
                       discard = "none")  # Don't discard unmatched individuals

# Extract matched data, including unmatched individuals
nhefs$weights_matched <- match_model$weights  # Matched individuals will have weight > 0, unmatched will have 0

### (B) Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW)

# Calculate IPW weights for the entire dataset
nhefs$ipw_weights <- ifelse(nhefs$qsmk == 1, 1 / nhefs$pscore, 1 / (1 - nhefs$pscore))

# Survey design object for weighted analysis
design_ipw <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~ipw_weights, data = nhefs)

### (C) Calculate Standardized Mean Differences (SMDs)

# 1. Unmatched SMD (for the full cohort, no weights)
balance_unmatched <- bal.tab(qsmk ~ sex + race + age + education + smokeintensity + smokeyrs +
                             exercise + active + wt71 + hbp, data = nhefs, estimand = "ATT", 
                             method = NULL)
smd_unmatched <- as.data.frame(balance_unmatched$Balance)

# 2. Matched SMD (including unmatched individuals with zero weights)
balance_matched <- bal.tab(qsmk ~ sex + race + age + education + smokeintensity + smokeyrs +
                           exercise + active + wt71 + hbp, weights = nhefs$weights_matched, data = nhefs, 
                           estimand = "ATT", method = "weighting")
smd_matched <- as.data.frame(balance_matched$Balance)

# 3. IPW SMD (IPW using the entire cohort)
balance_ipw <- bal.tab(qsmk ~ sex + race + age + education + smokeintensity + smokeyrs +
                       exercise + active + wt71 + hbp, weights = nhefs$ipw_weights, data = nhefs, 
                       estimand = "ATT", method = "weighting")
smd_ipw <- as.data.frame(balance_ipw$Balance)


# Ensure that all balance tables have the same covariates by selecting common rows
common_covariates <- intersect(intersect(rownames(smd_unmatched), rownames(smd_matched)), rownames(smd_ipw))

# Subset the balance tables to include only the common covariates
smd_unmatched <- smd_unmatched[common_covariates, ]
smd_matched <- smd_matched[common_covariates, ]
smd_ipw <- smd_ipw[common_covariates, ]

### (D) Prepare Data for Plotting

# Extract SMDs from the balance tables
smd_data <- data.frame(
  Covariate = common_covariates,
  Unweighted_SMD = smd_unmatched$Diff.Un,
  Matched_SMD = smd_matched$Diff.Adj,
  Weighted_SMD = smd_ipw$Diff.Adj
)

# Reshape data to long format using pivot_longer from tidyr
smd_data_long <- smd_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Unweighted_SMD", "Matched_SMD", "Weighted_SMD"), 
               names_to = "SMD_Type", values_to = "SMD_Value")

### (E) Plot the SMDs using ggplot2

ggplot(smd_data_long, aes(x = Covariate, y = SMD_Value, group = SMD_Type)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = SMD_Type), size = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = SMD_Type), size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Unweighted_SMD" = "red", "Matched_SMD" = "blue", "Weighted_SMD" = "green")) +
  labs(title = "Standardized Mean Differences Before and After Matching/Weighting",
       x = "Covariates",
       y = "Standardized Mean Difference (SMD)",
       color = "SMD Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


```
